title: Sessionization and aggregated curated tables for Console usage analytics
creator: Anika Rao
description: Goal: produce a set of curated, production-ready warehouse views/tables that power Console dashboards (usage, cost breakdowns, per-route latency percentiles), billing inputs, and alerting. Deliverables: 1) event_sessionized table (session-level joins across Console front-end events, API request logs, and model invocation records), 2) daily_rollup and weekly_aggregates for product metrics, 3) route_cost_attribution table that maps token-level cost to Console routes and features. This ticket covers schema decisions, transformations, backfill plan, QA queries, and a migration plan to switch dashboards from experimental denorm views to the curated tables.
background: Current state: several dashboards and billing reports rely on ad-hoc denormalized views and nightly Spark jobs. Those are brittle, cause duplicated logic in downstream queries, and make incremental backfills expensive. We need canonical, minimal-latency curated artifacts so Console teams and finance can rely on one source of truth.
design_decisions: Ingress model: keep raw events in raw_console_events (immutable, partitioned by ingest_date) and build curated artifacts in curated_console.events_sessionized.
Sessionization window: 30-minute inactivity threshold for user sessions; session_id generated using user_id + session_start_ts hash to ensure idempotent recompute.
Join strategy: prefer event-time joins with watermarks in Spark/Beam to reduce mis-joins; for backfills use deterministic hash-based partitioning to parallelize safely.

Token cost attribution: derive per-invocation token counts from model_invocations stream and map to route via request_id; use model pricing lookup table to compute USD cost at ingestion time and store both raw_tokens and cost_usd to facilitate currency re-eval without touching raw events.

Retention & partitioning: curated tables partitioned by event_date with monthly clustered columns on org_id, project_id for common filter patterns. Keep 365-day retention for curated artifacts with ability to rehydrate from raw events for older windows.
Performance: implement incremental materialized views for daily_rollup and hourly_ingest_aggregates. Materialization strategy will use merge-on-write to keep costs predictable.
Schema contract: explicit typed columns (iso timestamps, strings for enums) and a __source_version column so we can evolve transforms safely and track which code produced each row.

Backfill approach: staged backfill starting with last 90 days in compute cluster, validate against current dashboards, then expand to full 365 days if validated. Backfill jobs will be idempotent and emit a backfill_manifest file to GCS with checksums.
Observability: emit lineage and row-counts to telemetry topic for SLO monitoring; add anomaly detector on daily_ingested_tokens and new_org_count.
Privacy: PII fields (user_email, ip) will be hashed or redacted in curated tables per data governance guidance; raw_console_events remains in a restricted dataset.
Migration: Console dashboards will be migrated to curated_console.* views behind a feature flag. Keep old views for 30 days after migration and run comparison queries nightly.
Failure modes: if cost lookup fails for a given model version, mark cost_usd as UNKNOWN and route to a resolution queue; do not drop the row to maintain fidelity for event counts.
Access: curated_console dataset ACLs restricted to analytics and console-backend service accounts; finance_read role will have read-only access to route_cost_attribution.
Testing: unit tests for transforms, integration tests against a synthetic event corpus, and a dashboard-level diff test comparing old and new rollups within tolerance thresholds.
Query patterns: optimize for queries that slice by org_id + date range + route_name and provide pre-aggregates for top-10 routes to keep interactive dashboard latency below 2s.
Storage budget: capped daily compute budget for materializations; use compression and parquet/replication settings to meet storage targets.
Ownership: analytics-platform owns ETL pipelines, Console PM/BI owns downstream dashboard mapping and acceptance criteria.
Tooling: implement transforms in Beam on Dataflow (preferred) or Spark as fallback; CI jobs will validate schema using continuous integration checks in GitHub.
APIs & references: we'll publish a contracts doc in Confluence and a JSON schema descriptor in the repo for consumers.
Rollout plan: small test orgs first (5 orgs), then staged increase to 50, 500, then all orgs contingent on SLI checks.
Cost smoothing: implement a 7-day rolling average column for token_cost volatility smoothing in finance views.
Fallback: if materialization fails, dashboards should fallback to last successful snapshot and emit an incident ticket automatically.
Data freshness target: curated tables should be available within 30 minutes of event arrival for recent traffic; daily_rollup available within 2 hours.
Idempotency: all transforms will be idempotent with dedupe keys to prevent double-counting on retries.
acceptance_criteria: events_sessionized exists with documented schema and sample rows and matches reference queries for user session counts within 0.1% vs current denorm views for last 30 days.
route_cost_attribution returns consistent token and USD totals for three test orgs and matches finance ground truth within tolerance.
daily_rollup and weekly_aggregates materializations run on schedule and complete within budgeted compute time for average traffic.
Migration feature flag toggles dashboards to curated views for canary orgs and nightly diff job shows no regressions.
Backfill manifest generated and validated checksums for backfilled partitions; backfill window validated against acceptance queries.
End-to-end tests in CI validate schema and a synthetic smoke test that simulates concurrent ingestion and recompute paths.
Access controls validated and documented; finance team granted read-only access to route_cost_attribution.
Runbooks updated for common failure modes and on-call knows how to triage pipeline stalls or cost lookup failures.
implementation_steps: Draft schema and JSON contract and review with Console PM and Finance.
Implement Beam transform for sessionization and token-cost enrichment in repo analytics/console/transform/.
Add unit/integration tests and CI checks for schema validation.
Deploy nightly backfill job for last 90 days to staging dataset.
Run comparison queries and iterate on bugs found by Console PM.
Enable feature flag for canary orgs and run 7-day smoke validation.
Schedule progressive rollout and finalize dashboards migration.
Tidy up old denorm views and decommission after 30-day overlap.
Postmortem and lessons learned checklist after rollout complete.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect sessionization leads to under/over-counting of MAU. Mitigation: run side-by-side comparisons and tune inactivity threshold; add TTL-based session collapse for bots.
Risk: Cost lookup lag produces UNKNOWN costs. Mitigation: add queued reconciliation job and flag rows for finance review rather than dropping.
Risk: High compute cost for backfill. Mitigation: stage backfills, use spot workers, and cap parallelism per project.
Risk: Dashboard regressions during migration. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout with nightly diffs and rollback plan.
